title: Bulk gDNA Extraction from Coral Samples
author: Andrew Baker
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.dyq7vv

steps.title: Collect coral tissue sample
steps.instruction: Obtain a small amount of coral tissue (branch tip clipping, razor‑blade scraping, or biopsy) without skeleton; if using larger core fragments, blast tissue off the skeleton with an airbrush or Water Pik, centrifuge the blastate and proceed to lysis.

steps.title: Lyse tissue in SDS buffer
steps.instruction: Place the sample in a microcentrifuge tube containing 500 µL of 1 % SDS in DNA Buffer (DNAB); ensure the sample is fully immersed and incubate at 65 °C for 60–90 min. The lysate can be stored at room temperature as an “archive”.

steps.title: Add Proteinase K and digest
steps.instruction: Add 25 µL Proteinase K (10 mg mL⁻¹) to the archived lysate, vortex, then incubate under one of the following conditions: overnight at 37 °C, 6–7 h at 45 °C, or 2–3 h at 55 °C.

steps.title: Aliquot sample archive
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes, transfer 100 µL of the sample archive (1 % SDS in DNAB) to each tube, and return the remaining archive to storage. Volumes may be scaled proportionally for later steps.

steps.title: Add CTAB mix and incubate
steps.instruction: Defrost CTAB mix (stored at –20 °C), add 200 µL (twice the sample volume) to each tube, vortex, and incubate at 65 °C for 30–60 min.

steps.title: Extract with chloroform
steps.instruction: Allow samples to cool, then in a fume hood add 300 µL chloroform (equal volume to the sample). Before first use, charge the pipette tip by filling and emptying it 2–3 times. Vortex, invert several times with caps tightly sealed, and place the tubes on a rotating platform for 2–3 h.

steps.title: Phase separation by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 10 000 g (RCF) for 10 min with tube hinges outward. While spinning, label a new set of 1.5 mL tubes. After spin, carefully pipette the top ~250 µL aqueous phase into a new tube and discard the remainder.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL (twice the aqueous volume) of 100 % (200‑proof) ethanol (Omnipure Catalog #4455) to each tube, seal caps tightly, and invert several times with brief shakes to mix.

steps.title: Freeze for DNA precipitation
steps.instruction: Place tubes in a –20 °C freezer for at least 2 h (if ethanol is pre‑chilled, 0.5 h is sufficient) to promote DNA precipitation.

steps.title: Centrifuge to pellet DNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 10 000 g (RCF) for 10 min with hinges outward.

steps.title: Remove super‑ethanol
steps.instruction: Decant the ethanol supernatant into waste; the DNA pellet remains adhered to the tube wall.

steps.title: Dry pellet in SpeedVac
steps.instruction: Place tubes (caps open) in a Vacufuge/SpeedVac, avoiding contact with the inside of caps, and dry at 45 °C for 30–60 min.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in NaOAc
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of 0.3 M sodium acetate (do not use the 3 M stock), vortex until the pellet dissolves into a syrupy solution.

steps.title: Second ethanol precipitation
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of 100 % ethanol, vortex and invert several times, then freeze at –20 °C for at least 2 h.

steps.title: Centrifuge and discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 10 000 g (RCF) for 10 min, then decant the supernatant into waste.

steps.title: Wash pellet with 70 % ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of 70 % ethanol, vortex thoroughly, centrifuge at 10 000 g for 10 min, and decant the wash liquid.

steps.title: Final drying in SpeedVac
steps.instruction: Place tubes (caps open) in the Vacufuge and dry at 45 °C for 30–60 min to remove residual ethanol.

steps.title: Re‑suspend DNA in TE buffer
steps.instruction: Add 50–100 µL TE buffer, vortex briefly to mix, and store the DNA at –20 °C. The sample is now ready for PCR.
